children: AI infrastructure demand tightens memory chip supplies, pushing global smartphone prices higher and forcing manufacturers to prioritise profitability over shipment volumes

Global smartphone shipments fell 20 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, reaching their lowest level for the period since 2012, as memory chip shortages and rising component costs squeezed manufacturers, according to media reports.

The supply crunch, driven by intense demand for memory components from artificial intelligence infrastructure projects, has pushed manufacturers to raise retail prices and scale back shipments. Global smartphone retail prices have risen 20 per cent so far in 2026, adding to affordability pressures and widening the gap between premium and price-sensitive market segments.
AI Infrastructure Demand Deepens Memory Shortage

Rising prices of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash components have increased smartphone production costs, while limited supplies have disrupted shipments across manufacturers. According to media reports, the third quarter was the second consecutive quarter to bear the full impact of the memory shortage.

Manufacturers are passing higher component costs on to consumers, contributing to a 20 per cent increase in global smartphone retail prices so far this year. The pressure is particularly acute in lower-priced segments, where higher prices can make device upgrades less affordable and constrain demand.

The shift in consumer behaviour is reinforcing manufacturers’ focus on profitability rather than shipment volumes. While demand for premium devices has remained comparatively resilient, higher prices and limited component availability are putting additional pressure on the mass market.
Samsung Retains Lead As Apple’s Share Reaches 22 Per Cent

Samsung remained the world’s largest smartphone vendor in the third quarter, with a 23 per cent market share, even as its shipments declined 3 per cent year-on-year. Demand for its Galaxy Z Fold8 series and stable component supplies for its mid-range devices supported its performance, according to media reports.

Apple’s market share reached 22 per cent, crossing the 20 per cent threshold for the first time in a third quarter, despite a year-on-year decline in shipments. Counterpoint attributed the decline partly to the absence of a base iPhone 18 model, which resulted in a smaller launch-month channel fill than the full iPhone 17 lineup a year earlier.

The iPhone 18 Pro models recorded a stronger launch than their predecessors, particularly in China and India, while continued momentum from the iPhone 17 series helped offset the shipment decline, Counterpoint said in its market assessment.
Xiaomi, OPPO And vivo Face Shipment Declines

Xiaomi’s smartphone shipments fell more than 30 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter, taking its market share to 10 per cent. The company reduced its exposure to lower-priced devices and some overseas markets while tightening shipment plans to protect margins amid rising memory costs.

OPPO and vivo recorded shipment declines exceeding 20 per cent, with their market shares falling to 9 per cent and 8 per cent, respectively. Counterpoint’s OPPO grouping includes OnePlus and realme, so the figures cover those brands as well.

Both manufacturers raised prices across their entry-level and mid-range portfolios in response to higher memory costs. OPPO also consolidated its portfolio and operations across OPPO, realme and OnePlus to reduce overlap and improve cost efficiency, while vivo prioritised its core India and China markets.
Premium Devices Gain Strategic Importance

The divergence between premium and price-sensitive segments is reshaping manufacturers’ product and market strategies. Samsung’s stronger position in higher-value devices and Apple’s share gains illustrate how premium portfolios can support market positioning even when overall shipment volumes decline.

At the same time, price increases are pushing some budget models out of established price bands, while component shortages constrain the availability of devices. Xiaomi has also continued to strengthen its presence in China’s upper-mid-range and premium segments, according to Counterpoint Research.
Smartphone Market Outlook Remains Challenging

Counterpoint Research expects difficult conditions to persist through the remainder of 2026, with production cuts, narrower product portfolios and a greater focus on premium devices likely to continue. Elevated component costs and limited supplies are expected to keep pressure on price-sensitive segments. The market’s recovery will depend in part on memory availability, component pricing and manufacturers’ ability to balance profitability with demand. For smartphone makers, protecting margins while maintaining competitive prices is likely to remain a central challenge as the memory shortage continues.
